newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga, Telekom fall on industry-change worries.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga, Telekom fall on industry-change worries.

text.p: The stocks of market heavyweights Tenaga Nasional Bhd and Telekom Malaysia Bhd continued to fall in the afternoon on worries over changes within their industries, analysts said.
Around 0810 GMT, Tenaga was down 60 cents to 12.30 and Telekm by 40 cents to 20.20. Dealers said the selling was led by foreign institutions.
Tenaga fell as low as 12.00 ringgit on worries that it could lose its distribution monopoly, analysts said.

Local newspaper reports on Tuesday said the government had awarded licences to a consortium of companies to generate, distribute and sell electricity to companies operating in an industrial park in the northern Malaysian state of Kedah.
"This is the first case where a company is licenced to generate for customers," said ING-Barings analyst Yap Huey Chiang.

But other analysts said there were other "special case" projects where power generation and distribution would be carried out by companies other than Tenaga, such as the new Kuala Lumpur international airport and an integrated complex named Kuala Lumpur Sentral.
Analysts said there were worries that the Kedah project may see other distribution licences being awarded to other companies in large upcoming projects.
Telekom's fall was linked to speculation that industry deregulation would be brought forward, ahead of a January 1, 1999 deadline agreed upon by industry players.

Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie hinted on Monday that the advent of equal access to several fixed line service operators for consumers would be welcomed by his office. Analysts said the move would hurt Telekom Malaysia, which currently enjoys a near monopoly over the local and international fixed line service.
An analyst said that the sell-off on Telekom was "an excuse to further download on Telekom stock".
